test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 14 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Pulakeshin II was the famous ruler of which of the following dynasties?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chalukya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pulakeshin II was one of the most prominent rulers of the **Chalukya dynasty**, which ruled large parts of southern and central India.
 
• He reigned during the early 7th century CE (circa 610-642 CE) and is best known for his military conquests and administrative capabilities.
 
• Pulakeshin II successfully repelled the northward expansion of **Harsha**, the ruler of Kannauj, in a significant battle near the Narmada River.
 
• He expanded the Chalukya Empire significantly, establishing control over Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh regions.
 
• The **Aihole inscription**, composed by his court poet Ravikirti, provides detailed accounts of his conquests and achievements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chalukya Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Chalukyas were divided into three branches: the Early Chalukyas (Badami Chalukyas), the Western Chalukyas, and the Eastern Chalukyas.
 
• They made significant contributions to art, architecture, and administration, including iconic temples at Badami, Aihole, and Pattadakal.
 
 
 
• **Aihole Inscription:**
 
 
• It is a Sanskrit inscription in Kannada script that details Pulakeshin II's victories and his valor.
 
• The inscription also describes Pulakeshin II as a great patron of culture and a skilled administrator.
 
 
 
• **Harsha:**
 
 
• He was a powerful ruler of northern India during the 7th century, and his empire extended across much of the Gangetic plain.
 
• His defeat by Pulakeshin II marked the southern boundary of his empire.
 
 
 
• **Pattadakal Temples:**
 
 
• Pattadakal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, showcases the architectural brilliance of the Chalukyas under Pulakeshin II's reign.
 
• These temples represent a fusion of Dravidian and Nagara architectural styles.
